replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

content.text:
<system-reminder>
Codebase and user instructions are shown below. Be sure to adhere to these instructions. IMPORTANT: These instructions OVERRIDE any default behavior and you MUST follow them exactly as written.

Contents of /home/runner/work/codeReader/codeReader/work/openinfer-project-openinfer/CLAUDE.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):

This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Lines gated on their own kernel feature need it named to run their unit tests.
# The K3 command also names the kernels crate, whose K3 tests ride the same
# feature:
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-k3 -p pegainfer-kernels --features k3 --lib
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-glm52 --features glm52 --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

# Team Documentation Workflow

Collaboration centered on the `docs/` directory.

## Knowledge Architecture (domain-axis)

Docs are organized by what they're *about*, not by lifecycle stage. A doc's freshness lives in its TL;DR (and `Last touched:` for active areas) — not by which directory it sits in. Completed work stays co-located with its domain. There is no `archives/` directory — if a doc no longer earns its keep, delete it; if a lasting lesson hides inside it, lift that lesson into `lessons/` first, then delete.

```
docs/
├── index.md           # Routing table — every doc must be listed here
├── roadmap/           # Strategic plans, quarterly direction, milestones
├── models/<line>/     # Per-model living docs (qwen3, qwen35, kimi-k2, ...)
│                      # — design, accuracy, perf, refactor records, gotchas
├── subsystems/<area>/ # Cross-cutting components (runtime, scheduler, frontend, kernels)
├── playbooks/         # Reusable how-to: benching, profiling, accuracy, onboarding
├── lessons/           # Tribal knowledge from research / other projects
├── benchmarks/        # Standalone benchmark snapshots and eval reports
├── conventions/       # Ongoing standards (bench regression, coding style)
└── private/           # Local-only notes (gitignored)
```

Classification rule at capture time:
- Is it tied to a specific model? → `models/<line>/`
- A specific subsystem? → `subsystems/<area>/`
- Reusable how-to applicable across models? → `playbooks/`
- Lasting lesson from elsewhere (other repo, research, postmortem)? → `lessons/`
- Snapshot of measurement, not a doc that evolves? → `benchmarks/`
- Strategic / cross-cutting plan? → `roadmap/`

If you can't pick one, the doc probably needs splitting.

## Documentation Style

- Docs cover what `--help` and code can't: pitfalls, diagnostic paths, decision context. Don't restate CLI reference.
- Every command in a doc must be run and verified before committing. Unverified commands are technical debt.
- The only required header is a one-line **TL;DR**. Keep it true; that's the contract.
- For `models/<line>/` and `subsystems/<area>/` docs, add `Last touched: YYYY-MM` and bump it when you do meaningful work on the doc (not for typo fixes). The date is a fact, not a judgement — readers infer freshness themselves.
- `playbooks/`, `lessons/`, `conventions/`, `roadmap/`, `benchmarks/`, `archives/` don't need a freshness stamp. They're either timeless until disproven, or self-dated, or explicitly inert.
- No `Status:` enum. Enum fields go stale exactly when you need them most.

## index.md Drift Policy

`index.md` is a routing table with a scanning-friendly TL;DR column. It is *allowed to drift* from the TL;DR inside each doc — the doc body is authoritative. Update `index.md` when you create or delete a doc, or when the existing TL;DR is so wrong it actively misleads. Don't churn it on every doc edit.

## Core Principles (CODE)

Documentation exists to advance work, not to hoard information. Four steps when handling information:

1. **Capture**: Only record what materially advances the project. When in doubt, leave it out.
2. **Organize**: Action-oriented. Resist the urge to organize for organization's sake — structure should be just enough.
3. **Distill**: Refactor over append. When you learn something new or hit a pitfall, integrate it into the document body — don't pile a changelog at the bottom.
4. **Express**: Every document must point to a next step. Split unwieldy documents proactively. Active documents must note the current blocker or next action.

## Collaboration Lifecycle

**Sync**

At the start of each session, you must read `index.md` and load the documents needed for the task at hand.

**Execute**
- Update relevant documents as you go. When a new problem or idea arises, create a document in the appropriate domain directory (see classification rule above).
- Record *why* a decision was made, not just *what* was done.

**Commit**

When a session wraps up:
- Update the TL;DR (and `Last touched`, where applicable) at the top of each modified document.
- Update `index.md` only when you created or deleted a doc, or when its TL;DR row is now misleading (see Drift Policy above).

## 前置讲义摘要（你必须基于这些已建立的认知继续，不要重复，要承接）

### u1-l1 crate 定位与模块地图：pegainfer-qwen3 是什么

本讲确立 pegainfer-qwen3 的定位：它是 PegaInfer（纯 Rust+CUDA、全程无 Python 的推理引擎）中 Qwen3 模型线的模型 crate；「默认模型线」来自服务器 crate 的默认 feature 与工作区 default-members 的叠加，故 stock build 只编译 Qwen3，而本 crate 自身无默认 feature，仅有内核报告等工具性开关。核心结论：lib.rs 的 25 个模块可归为配置、权重、前向执行、调度、执行器、投机解码、LoRA、KV 数据面、契约接入、诊断十层；model_line 面向 CLI，frontend_adapter 承接引擎契约，scheduler 是不含契约的纯调度。引入的关键术语：prefill/decode 两阶段；plan/result 相位边界（纯数据、不含引擎句柄，使决策与执行解耦）；runtime 再导出层即公共执行边界——Qwen3Executor 与三对计划/结果类型由此暴露，调度器与模型本地基准共用该入口，服务器则走高层 launch。
### u1-l2 运行与测试地图：单测、GPU 集成测试与测试夹具

本讲梳理 pegainfer-qwen3 的测试地图，覆盖四个最小模块：一、`--lib` 单测——`#[cfg(test)]` 模块测纯 CPU 逻辑（配置、调度装箱等），无 GPU 即可跑；空 feature `test-fixtures` 经 dev-dependency 自引用，只向测试编译暴露夹具。二、clean skip 模式——`model_path_or_skip()` 读 `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH`，否则探测默认模型路径，缺权重时打印说明并跳过而非失败，优于 `#[ignore]`。三、hf_golden_gate 数值门——以 HuggingFace 为真值，teacher-forcing 逐位置对比 logprobs；它绕过调度器与 frontend，直接用 `runtime` 再导出的 `Qwen3Executor` 和 plan/result 类型，所有 pass 串在一个 `#[test]` 里独占显存。四、`tests/common/harness.rs`——泵线程把 step 批量更新按请求 id 解复用进 Inbox+Condvar 队列，还原 submit/recv/expect_finished 的每请求阻塞流。核心结论：测试分层让无 GPU 的贡献者也能跑通绝大多数回归。承接概念：cfg(test) 与 feature 的边界、teacher-forcing、bf16 的 ULP 漂移（容差设计后续专讲）。
### u1-l3 ModelLine：Qwen3 如何挂进服务器 CLI

本讲剖析 Qwen3 如何挂进服务器 CLI。核心概念是 ModelLine trait（「模型线」＝一个模型家族的全部服务侧知识），以 8 个 hook 构成模型 crate 与纯派发服务器之间的唯一接缝，hook 按服务器启动时序依次调用。三个最小模块：Qwen3Cli（13 个专属 flag，含本讲新增的 EAGLE-3 草稿模型路径）、Qwen3Line::validate（15 条跨标志互斥规则）、Qwen3Line::launch（把 CLI 值与共享 flag 纯翻译成 Qwen3LaunchOptions，交给 crate::launch）。关键机制：consume-or-reject——共享 flag 按线认领，未认领而显式提供即拒绝；arg_requirements——按使用触发的声明式依赖，可级联；两者都以 provided（显式提供）为语义基准，默认值永不触发。互斥规则的根源是 LoRA、批不变、草稿器、decode-overlap、TP 各自独占 GPU 的同段资源；validate 的块序即报错优先级；DFlash 与 EAGLE-3 草稿器（分别走共享与专属 flag）在 crate::launch 被折叠为二选一的 Option\<DraftModel\>。核心结论：同一不变量多层设防，失败越早越便宜；启动策略归模型 crate，不泄漏进服务器。
### u1-l4 引擎契约与启动装配：frontend_adapter 全景

本讲覆盖 Qwen3 对接引擎契约的三个最小模块：launch 启动策略、start_qwen3 装配执行器、start_with_executor 铸造 Engine 并拉起调度线程。核心结论：契约三件套中 Engine 交出调度线程句柄与元数据，Scheduler 被驱动线程轮询 submit/step/metrics，RequestLedger 由驱动侧拥有、按 RequestId 记录裁定与 token；frontend_adapter 只承担账本写入与引擎装配两项契约职责。launch 把 DFlash 与 EAGLE-3 两条草稿路径折叠成互斥的单槽 DraftModel（两者共享目标隐藏态捕获管线与显存预留）。构建后三旋钮顺序不可乱：关前缀缓存、开 decode 重叠、最后装草稿，因装载草稿会强制关闭前缀缓存。关键术语：max_draft_batch 能力位（DFlash 不限、EAGLE-3 仅批一）、DeferredFinish 延迟完成、ModelExecutor 抽象与九段式 step，为 u2-u4 与 u6 铺路。

本讲剖析 Qwen3 crate 的 executor.rs，即真正执行一步前向的层次。核心结论：调度器与执行器之间只以三组纯数据 plan→result（prefill/decode/unified）交换信息——plan 借用 StepItem 切片，result 拥有新算出的 token 与 logprob；unified 把 prefill 行与 decode 行拼进同一次前向与 GEMM。ModelExecutor trait 是调度器对执行器的全部认知，也是与模型本地 benchmark 共用的相位边界；调度器按它泛型化，可用 FakeExecutor 做 CPU 单测。RequestId 端到端不变量：submit 时铸造，原样贯穿所有队列、effect 与 KV 键，无第二 id 空间。引入的关键概念：StepItem 是双向信封，executor 回填 cached_tokens 等三态字段；draft_context_captured_requests 是投机解码唯一的批级 result 字段，折入 draft_ready_requests 集合，普通 decode 步将其作废；ConnectorLookupCounters 以咨询标记加恰好一次结算记录外部 KV 查找账；max_draft_batch 是草稿器能力位，DFlash 不限、EAGLE-3 仅单请求，调度批宽门据此把宽批退回纯解码，输出无损。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. - "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))

1	//! DFlash prefill-capture eligibility predicates.
2	//!
3	//! A request can seed the DFlash draft only if its prefill produces clean target
4	//! hidden states: no LoRA, no prefix-cache hit, no prompt logprobs, no
5	//! completion logprobs. Sampling params are irrelevant here — the prompt's
6	//! hidden states are sampling-independent, and sampled-verify (#512) speculates
7	//! the full sampling surface, so capture is as valid for a sampled request as
8	//! for a greedy one.
9	
10	use super::PrefillStepItem;
11	use super::RequestId;
12	
13	/// Whether a prefill produces clean target hidden states to seed a drafter
14	/// (DFlash and EAGLE-3 alike).
15	pub(super) fn prefill_capture_supported(req: &PrefillStepItem) -> bool {
16	    req.lora_adapter.is_none()
17	        && req.cached_tokens.unwrap_or(0) == 0
18	        && req.logprobs.is_none()
19	        && req.prompt_logprobs.is_none()
20	}
21	
22	/// Eligible AND continuous: either the first chunk, or a later chunk whose
23	/// earlier chunks already captured context (no gaps in the pending buffer).
24	pub(super) fn dflash_prefill_can_capture(
25	    req: &PrefillStepItem,
26	    pending_state_exists: bool,
27	) -> bool {
28	    prefill_capture_supported(req) && (req.chunk_start == 0 || pending_state_exists)
29	}
30	
31	/// Capture hidden states during this prefill step iff any request is eligible.
32	pub(super) fn should_capture_dflash_prefill_context(
33	    requests: &[PrefillStepItem],
34	    pending_state_exists: impl Fn(RequestId) -> bool,
35	) -> bool {
36	    !requests.is_empty()
37	        && requests
38	            .iter()
39	            .any(|req| dflash_prefill_can_capture(req, pending_state_exists(req.request_id)))
40	}
41	
42	/// What to do with a request's DFlash state after a prefill step.
43	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
44	pub(super) enum DFlashPrefillAction {
45	    /// Context captured and prefill finished → ready to draft.
46	    MarkReady,
47	    /// Context captured but more chunks remain → keep the pending state.
48	    KeepPending,
49	    /// Ineligible → drop any stale state.
50	    Drop,
51	}
52	
53	pub(super) fn dflash_prefill_action(
54	    captured_context: bool,
55	    completed: bool,
56	) -> DFlashPrefillAction {
57	    match (captured_context, completed) {
58	        (true, true) => DFlashPrefillAction::MarkReady,
59	        (true, false) => DFlashPrefillAction::KeepPending,
60	        (false, _) => DFlashPrefillAction::Drop,
61	    }
62	}
63

66	    use super::*;
67

70	        assert_eq!(
71	            dflash_prefill_action(true, true),
72	            DFlashPrefillAction::MarkReady
73	        );
74	        assert_eq!(
75	            dflash_prefill_action(true, false),
76	            DFlashPrefillAction::KeepPending
77	        );
78	        assert_eq!(

81	        );

4	//! plain decode runs the decode kernel, and the two differ by about one bf16
5	//! ULP, so an exact `spec == baseline` match false-fails on a benign tie flip.
6	//! At the first divergence the check re-prefills the shared context and accepts
7	//! the speculative pick only when it sits within `MARGIN_TOL` of that prefill
8	//! argmax.

11	// different slice of it.

21	/// Top-K logprobs requested from the baseline; wide enough that the speculative
22	/// pick is in the set on any real tie (a pick outside the top-K is itself a red
23	/// flag the gate should catch).

25	/// Max acceptable regret: how far below the baseline's argmax (in the baseline's
26	/// own logprobs) the speculative pick may sit at the divergence point. ~3 bf16
27	/// ULP at typical logit magnitudes — mirrors `hf_golden_gate`'s `MARGIN_TOL`.
28	pub(crate) const MARGIN_TOL: f32 = 0.20;

30	/// One decoded position: the chosen token and (when requested) the top-K
31	/// `(token, logprob)` distribution that produced it.
32	pub(crate) struct Step {
33	    pub(crate) id: u32,
34	    pub(crate) top_logprobs: Vec<(u32, f32)>,
35	}

37	/// Fold a finished request's outcome into decoded steps: tokens paired with
38	/// their requested top-K distributions (empty when logprobs were off).
39	pub(crate) fn to_steps(outcome: Outcome) -> Vec<Step> {
40	    let Outcome {
41	        tokens, logprobs, ..
42	    } = outcome;
43	    tokens
44	        .into_iter()
45	        .enumerate()
46	        .map(|(i, id)| Step {
47	            id,
48	            top_logprobs: logprobs
49	                .get(i)
50	                .and_then(Option::as_ref)
51	                .map(|lp| lp.top_logprobs.clone())
52	                .unwrap_or_default(),
53	        })
54	        .collect()
55	}

57	/// Submit one greedy request and collect the decoded steps until it finishes.
58	pub(crate) fn generate(
59	    engine: &EngineHarness,
60	    prompt_tokens: Vec<u32>,
61	    logprobs: usize,
62	    max_tokens: usize,
63	) -> Vec<Step> {
64	    let mut req = request(prompt_tokens, SamplingParams::default(), max_tokens);
65	    req.logprobs = (logprobs > 0).then_some(logprobs);
66	    to_steps(engine.submit(req).expect_finished())

71	/// the reference the spec pick should match (vs the plain-decode baseline, whose
72	/// kernel resolves bifurcation ties to the other side). Returns the first
73	/// generated token's `(id, top_logprobs)`.
74	fn prefill_next(engine: &EngineHarness, context: Vec<u32>, logprobs: usize) -> Step {
75	    let mut req = request(context, SamplingParams::default(), 1);
76	    req.logprobs = (logprobs > 0).then_some(logprobs);
77	    req.prompt_logprobs = Some(logprobs);

95	    tokenizer: &DynTokenizer,

97	    prompt: &str,
98	    prompt_tokens: &[u32],
99	    base: &[Step],

101	) -> Result<(), String> {

103	        .iter()
104	        .zip(spec)
105	        .take_while(|(b, s)| b.id == s.id)
106	        .count();

109	    if matched == base.len().min(spec.len()) {

122	    }
123	
124	    let spec_id = spec[matched].id;
125	    let decode_argmax = base[matched].top_logprobs[0].0;
126	
127	    // Diagnostic: show the exact branch point.
128	    {
129	        let lo = matched.saturating_sub(2);
130	        let hi = (matched + 3).min(base.len()).min(spec.len());
131	        let base_ids: Vec<u32> = base[..hi].iter().map(|s| s.id).collect();

133	        eprintln!(
134	            "  [diag] context+gen base ids {:?} = {:?}",
135	            base_ids,
136	            tokenizer.decode(&base_ids, false).unwrap_or_default()
137	        );
138	        eprintln!(
139	            "  [diag] base[{lo}..{hi}] = {:?}",
140	            base[lo..hi]
141	                .iter()
142	                .map(|s| (s.id, tokenizer.decode(&[s.id], false).unwrap_or_default()))
143	                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
144	        );
145	        eprintln!(
146	            "  [diag] spec[{lo}..{hi}] = {:?}",
147	            spec[lo..hi]
148	                .iter()
149	                .map(|s| (s.id, tokenizer.decode(&[s.id], false).unwrap_or_default()))
150	                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
151	        );
152	    }
153	
154	    // The verify path runs the prefill kernel, so the right reference for the
155	    // spec pick is a plain *prefill* of the same shared context — not the
156	    // plain-decode baseline, whose kernel resolves a bifurcation tie to the
157	    // other side and amplifies the gap.

168	            .find(|(t, _)| *t == spec_id)
169	            .map(|(_, lp)| base[matched].top_logprobs[0].1 - lp);
170	        eprintln!(

172	             decode→{decode_argmax}; spec matches prefill greedy (decode-margin {:?}). Not a spec bug.",
173	            decode_lp

176	    }

179	    // path builds its committed KV incrementally across batched speculative
180	    // spans while this reference prefill builds it in one shot; the two differ by

204	    // clearly below the prefill argmax — neither is a benign tie.

206	        .top_logprobs
207	        .iter()
208	        .find(|(t, _)| *t == spec_id)

1	//! Method-agnostic core of **greedy** speculative decoding for Qwen3.
2	//!
3	//! Speculative decoding is an optimistic-concurrency transaction over the
4	//! decode loop: *propose* a span of `K` cheap draft tokens, *verify* them with a
5	//! single target forward over the `K + 1` span positions, *accept* the longest
6	//! prefix the target agrees with (plus one bonus token), then *commit* the
7	//! accepted KV and roll back the rejected draft KV. Only the **propose** step
8	//! varies between methods (n-gram lookup, DFlash draft model, EAGLE, …); verify,
9	//! accept, and the KV transaction are shared.
10	//!
11	//! This module owns the shared half. The draft/verify boundary is a **pure
12	//! token span** — a model proposer's hidden states never cross it; they stay
13	//! inside the proposer (see [`crate::dflash`] and [`crate::eagle3`]). Both
14	//! proposers seed from target hidden states captured at prefill and verify,
15	//! so they share the capture, the ready set and this transaction; only the
16	//! worker lane that turns captures into drafts differs.
17	//!
18	//! Acceptance is [`accept_prefix_match`] for greedy and sampled requests alike
19	//! (#512, the sampled-verify mechanism GLM5.2 landed in #589): the verify
20	//! forward selects one *committed* token per span position — the fused argmax
21	//! for a greedy request, a regular per-row sample from the target distribution
22	//! for a non-greedy one — and the accepted prefix is simply the drafts that
23	//! match those tokens. For a deterministic (one-hot) draft this is lossless
24	//! speculative sampling: every committed token is a true sample from the
25	//! target distribution; acceptance only decides how many ride one step.

# 草稿车道集成与投机调优旋钮

> 讲义 id：u6-l7 · 层级：advanced · 依赖：u6-l2（DFlash 草稿模型）、u6-l6（verify 前向缓冲与分段 CUDA Graph）

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 解释 DFlash 草稿车道（lane）为什么必须与目标模型同住一条 worker 线程，以及「隐藏态不出车道」这条边界是如何在类型与借用结构上落实的。
2. 读懂 `dflash_prefill_action` 的三态决策表（MarkReady / KeepPending / Drop），并说出 `prefill_capture_supported` 在 af9e40e1 之后如何从 DFlash 专属谓词推广为两种草稿器（DFlash 与 EAGLE-3）共享的捕获资格判断。
3. 描述 `AutoHedge` 控制器的窗口化 explore-then-commit 设计：探索什么、按什么目标定价、如何提交、如何应对窗口污染与负载门打断。
4. 汇总全部投机旋钮（`PEGAINFER_SPEC_*` 环境变量与 `--dflash-draft-model-path` / `--eagle3-draft-model-path` CLI 标志）的作用面、默认值、读取时机与互斥规则，并理解 `spec_env` 为何对其中两个旋钮选择「坏值拒绝启动」而非静默回退。
5. 说明 `tests/common/lossless.rs` 抽出的共享无损性判定如何同时服务 DFlash 与 EAGLE-3 两个投机门测试。

## 2. 前置知识

- **车道（lane）与 worker 线程**（u3-l2）：`LocalQwen3Lane` 把一台 GPU 的全部可变状态打包，独占一条 worker 线程；executor 线程通过 `StepCommand`（算什么）与 `WorkerCommand`（控制面）两条通道与它通信。本讲的「草稿车道」就住在这个结构里。
- **投机解码事务**（u6-l1）：propose → verify → accept → commit/rollback。草稿/验证边界是**纯 token 跨界**——proposer 的隐藏态不越线。本讲讲的是「线内」的那一侧。
- **draft_ready_requests 就绪集**（u3-l1/u4-l2）：executor 侧维护的「哪些请求已捕获目标隐藏态、可以进入草稿轮」集合；调度器的 `speculation_decision_at` 全有-or-全无门控以它为输入。
- **hedge（对冲）与 DSpark**（u6-l4）：在 DFlash backbone 上叠加 Markov 头后，可以同时在多个「第二名」分支上 rollout 多条草稿链，验证阶段并行展开。链数 `C` 是个难拍脑袋定的性能参数——这正是 4.3 节自定价控制器的动机。
- **OnceLock 一次性读取**：所有 `PEGAINFER_SPEC_*` 旋钮每个进程只读一次环境变量，之后缓存为静态值——运行中改环境变量不会生效。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 DFlashLaneState：草稿车道为何与目标同线程

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

「草稿车道」是 worker 线程里紧挨着目标模型的一块私有状态：草稿模型本身、每个请求的草稿态、批草稿 scratch、hedge 链与自定价控制器。它必须与目标模型同线程，原因是**草稿 rollout 直接读目标的词嵌入、输出头和捕获到的隐藏态**——这些张量体积大且生命周期归目标 lane 所有，跨线程搬运既要拷贝又破坏「纯 token 跨界」的事务边界。模块文档把这个设计写得很直白：

> 隐藏态是车道私有的（`pending_context`），从不跨到调度器一侧。[src/executor/dflash_lane.rs:L1-L7](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_lane.rs#L1-L7) 说明了这条边界。

af9e40e1 之后，`LocalQwen3Lane` 上有两个互斥的车道槽位——`dflash: Option<DFlashLaneState>` 与 `eagle3: Option<Eagle3LaneState>`，**至多一个被装载**（见 [src/executor.rs:L3410-L3414](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L3410-L3414) 的字段注释）。方法无关的那一半（捕获、ready 集、KV 事务）由 `speculative.rs` 共享，只有「把捕获变成草稿」的 worker 车道因草稿器而异——[src/speculative.rs:L11-L16](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/speculative.rs#L11-L16) 的模块文档明确了这个划分。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

一次投机轮在车道侧的时序：

```text
executor 线程                                worker 线程（primary lane）
─────────────                                ─────────────────────
StepCommand::SpeculativeDraft{requests} ───▶ 按 lane.eagle3.is_some() 分派：
                                              ├─ EAGLE-3 → execute_eagle3_draft
                                              └─ 否则    → execute_dflash_draft
                                                   1. take() 整个车道出 self（借用拆分）
                                                   2. 把批内所有请求的 state 从 HashMap 取出
                                                   3. 批量 backbone 前向 → scratch.logits
                                                   4. 提案路径三选一：
                                                      selector / markov(+hedge 阶梯) / 朴素 argmax
                                                   5. state 放回 HashMap，车道放回 self
                                                   6. 产出 [anchor, draft_1..draft_K]（纯 token）
◀── WorkerStepOutcome::SpeculativeDraft(result)
StepCommand::SpeculativeVerify{...}     ───▶ execute_draft_verify（u6-l6 的分段图路径）
                                              验证后捕获目标隐藏态 → record_verify_dflash_context
                                              （含 auto hedge 控制器的 tick / break_window）
```

装载侧：`WorkerCommand::LoadDflash` / `LoadEagle3` / `DropDraft` 三条控制面命令（[src/executor.rs:L4262-L4278](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L4262-L4278)）——装载必须在 worker 线程执行，因为草稿模型构建要读同线程的目标模型。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**车道结构体**——[src/executor/dflash_lane.rs:L29-L58](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_lane.rs#L29-L58) 定义 `DFlashLaneState`：`model`（草稿模型）、`requests`（每请求态的私有序表）、`scratch`（**车道级**批草稿缓冲，为整个 decode 批一次性分配，让稠密草稿算子整批跑一次而非每请求一次——u6-l2 讲过它）、验证/接受计数器、`hedge_blocks`、`auto` 控制器、`round_chains`，以及两 个「生效几何」字段 `hedge_cap` / `hedge_branch_positions`。

**生效几何只算一次**——[src/executor/dflash_lane.rs:L60-L102](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_lane.rs#L60-L102) 的 `new` 在构造期就把原始环境值解析成 `spec_hedge_effective`（按 block_size 过滤分支位置）并记日志。注释点名了动机：位置解析器会**静默丢弃不可解析项**，若不在启动时把生效几何打进日志，基准测试可能在比自己配置更窄的阶梯上测量。草稿路径、验证分派、控制器此后只读这两个字段，**永不重读原始环境值**（[src/executor/dflash_lane.rs:L50-L57](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_lane.rs#L50-L57) 的字段注释）。

**草稿轮主循环**——[src/executor/dflash_lane.rs:L286-L515](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_lane.rs#L286-L515) 的 `execute_dflash_draft`。两个结构技巧值得注意：

1. `self.dflash.take()` 把车道整体借出（[L294-L299](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_lane.rs#L294-L299)）：草稿前向借用 `dflash.model`/`dflash.scratch`，而朴素 argmax 路径要借用 `self.sample_scratch`，不 take 就撞 `self` 的借用冲突。
2. 所有请求的 state 先 `remove` 出 HashMap 再集体放回（[L300-L324](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_lane.rs#L300-L324)），让批量前向能同时持有全部 `&mut`。

链数决策的优先级在 [L375-L400](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_lane.rs#L375-L400)：`PEGAINFER_SPEC_HEDGE_KNEE` 的批自适应策略 **优先于** 固定链数与 auto 控制器；auto 模式下取 `controller.current_c().min(位置数)`。产出侧把 anchor 前置、按 `effective_drafts()` 截断（[L485-L510](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_lane.rs#L485-L510)）——这正是 `DraftMeta.num_spec_tokens` 所说的「span 恒为 K+1，anchor-first/anchor-drop 已折进草稿数」。

**跨草稿器分派**——[src/executor.rs:L534-L541](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L534-L541)：`StepCommand::SpeculativeDraft` 按 `lane.eagle3.is_some()` 分派到 EAGLE-3 或 DFlash 车道，二者产出同构的 `DraftResult`。

**装载分派与强制关前缀缓存**——[src/executor.rs:L1786-L1827](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L1786-L1827) 的 `load_draft_model` 接收 `DraftModel` 枚举（[src/speculative.rs:L33-L38](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/speculative.rs#L33-L38)），先拒绝多 rank 与 KV offload，再按变体走 `load_dflash` / `load_eagle3`，最后 `set_prefix_cache_enabled(false)`。结构性约束在 [src/executor.rs:L1702-L1709](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L1702-L1709)：`prefix_cache_enabled()` 返回 `requested && speculative.is_none()`——即使之后有人重新打开请求位，已装载的草稿器也让它保持关闭（前缀命中会跳过产出干净隐藏态的那次前向）。

**能力位上报**——`DraftMeta`（[src/executor.rs:L3372-L3388](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L3372-L3388)）新增 `max_draft_batch` 字段；trait 实现 [src/executor.rs:L2892-L2896](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L2892-L2896) 把它透出。DFlash 装载时填 `None`（不限），EAGLE-3 装载时填 `Some(EAGLE3_MAX_BATCH)` 即 `Some(1)`（[src/executor/eagle3_lane.rs:L62-L67](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/eagle3_lane.rs#L62-L67)）。调度门 [src/scheduler/plan.rs:L200-L204](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/scheduler/plan.rs#L200-L204) 据此把宽批退回纯解码（u4-l2 已讲判定路径，u6-l8 讲 EAGLE-3 车道全貌）。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `execute_dflash_draft` 不让调度器直接传「目标隐藏态」进来，而要车道自己在 prefill/verify 时捕获？

**答案**：因为草稿 rollout 读的是目标的词嵌入、输出头与捕获隐藏态，这些张量归目标 lane 所有且体积大；跨界搬运既拷贝昂贵，又破坏 speculative.rs 定下的「草稿/验证边界是纯 token 跨界」事务边界。隐藏态留在车道内（`pending_context`），调度器只见 token，这让事务核心与方法无关，也让 EAGLE-3 能直接换一条车道复用全部共享设施。

**练习 2**：`DFlashLaneState::new` 为什么要把 hedge 生效几何（`hedge_cap`/`hedge_branch_positions`）在构造期解析并打日志，而不是每次草稿轮重读环境变量？

**答案**：旋钮经 `OnceLock` 每进程只读一次，且位置解析器会静默丢弃不可解析条目并回退到位置 0——不在启动时把**生效**几何打进日志，基准测试可能在比自己以为更窄的阶梯上测量且无从发现。构造期一次性解析还保证草稿路径、验证分派、控制器三方读同一份几何，避免各自漂移（历史上「超出 block 的位置预留了永远用不上的页」正是两处漂移的产物）。

### 4.2 dflash_prefill_action：捕获资格与三态动作

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

投机解码的第一步是让草稿器拿到「种子」：目标模型在 prefill 时对每个 prompt token 产生的隐藏态。但不是每个 prefill 都能产出**干净**的隐藏态——LoRA 请求的隐藏态混入了适配器、前缀缓存命中跳过了部分前向、logprobs 评分改变了输出形状。`dflash_prefill.rs` 把「能不能捕」与「捕完怎么办」拆成两层谓词加一张三态表。

af9e40e1 的关键推广：原私有函数 `dflash_prefill_supported` 改名为 **`prefill_capture_supported`** 并提升为 `pub(super)`，文档注释从「捕获 DFlash 目标上下文」改为「产出干净目标隐藏态以播种草稿器（**DFlash 与 EAGLE-3 皆然**）」——EAGLE-3 车道的 `eagle3_prefill_eligible` 直接 import 它再叠加自己的贪心/整段约束（[src/executor/eagle3_lane.rs:L44-L53](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/eagle3_lane.rs#L44-L53)，详见 u6-l8）。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
prefill_capture_supported(req)          # 四条全过才算"干净"
  ├─ lora_adapter.is_none()             # LoRA 隐藏态混入适配器
  ├─ cached_tokens == 0                 # 前缀命中跳过了产生隐藏态的前向
  ├─ logprobs.is_none()                 # 补全 logprobs 改变输出形状
  └─ prompt_logprobs.is_none()          # 提示词评分同理
（注意：采样参数不是门 —— 隐藏态与采样无关，sampled-verify 使采样请求同样可投机）

dflash_prefill_can_capture(req, pending_exists)
  = prefill_capture_supported(req) && (chunk_start == 0 || pending_exists)
                                        # 首块，或前序块已捕获（无断链）

dflash_prefill_action(captured, completed):
  (true,  true ) → MarkReady     # 捕获完成且 prefill 结束 → 进 ready 集
  (true,  false) → KeepPending   # 捕获了但还有后续块 → 保持 pending
  (false, _    ) → Drop          # 不合格 → 丢弃陈旧 state
```

executor 侧消费点：prefill 结果回来后，对每个请求查 `draft_context_captured_requests` 是否包含它，套用三态表写 `draft_ready_requests` 集或发 `DropDraft` 命令清车道（[src/executor.rs:L2774-L2795](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L2774-L2795)）。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

- [src/executor/dflash_prefill.rs:L13-L20](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_prefill.rs#L13-L20)——推广后的 `prefill_capture_supported`，四条合取。模块文档（[L1-L8](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_prefill.rs#L1-L8)）解释了为什么采样参数被有意排除在门外。
- [src/executor/dflash_prefill.rs:L22-L40](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_prefill.rs#L22-L40)——`dflash_prefill_can_capture` 的连续性检查（断链的 pending 缓冲不能用），与批级 `should_capture_dflash_prefill_context` 的 any() 语义：批内**任一**请求合格，这次 prefill 步就开启捕获（捕获是整批一次的前向副产品）。
- [src/executor/dflash_prefill.rs:L42-L62](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_prefill.rs#L42-L62)——`DFlashPrefillAction` 枚举与纯函数决策表；配套单测 `prefill_action_table`（[L64-L87](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_prefill.rs#L64-L87)）逐一断言四个组合。
- 捕获记录与防错——`record_prefill_dflash_context`（[src/executor/dflash_lane.rs:L127-L194](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_lane.rs#L127-L194)）用 `ensure!` 钉死三条不变量：捕获行数必须等于调度 token 数、pending 长度必须等于 `chunk_start`（连续性）、不合格请求必须清 state。验证侧的 `record_verify_dflash_context`（[L199-L282](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_lane.rs#L199-L282)）只把**接受前缀**的隐藏态追加进 pending（被拒草稿的续写是错的），并在轮末驱动 auto hedge 控制器（[L270-L280](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_lane.rs#L270-L280)）。

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：一个带 `cached_tokens>0`（前缀缓存命中）的请求为什么必须 `Drop` 而不是「只捕后缀」？

**答案**：前缀命中意味着命中部分的目标前向被跳过，那段的隐藏态从未产生；草稿器需要的种子是**每个 prompt token** 的干净隐藏态。只有连续捕获（首块或 pending 存在的续块）才有效，断链的 pending 缓冲在 `record_prefill_dflash_context` 里会被 `pending_len == chunk_start` 的 ensure! 拒绝。这也解释了为什么装载草稿器会结构性关闭前缀缓存（4.1.3）。

**练习 2**：`prefill_capture_supported` 推广后，EAGLE-3 为什么还要在它之上叠加 `is_greedy() && chunk_start==0 && 整段` 三个条件？

**答案**：共享谓词回答的是「隐藏态干不干净」这个方法无关问题；EAGLE-3 v1 的前向实现有自己的额外假设——`prefill_prompt` 需要整段 prompt 一次建草稿 KV，链式 rollout 目前只支持贪心请求。所以 `eagle3_prefill_eligible = prefill_capture_supported ∧ 贪心 ∧ chunk_start==0 ∧ chunk 覆盖全 prompt ∧ ≥2 token`。共享的是「干净」语义，差异留在各自车道——这正是「共享捕获、ready 集与事务，只有 worker 车道不同」的落点。

### 4.3 auto hedge：窗口化 explore-then-commit 自定价

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

hedge 链数 `C` 是个尴尬的参数：最优值随流量形态漂移（难流量收敛到多链阶梯、易流量 `C=0` 最好），还受 CUDA Graph bucket 量化与 eager 惩罚影响，拍脑袋定死必然在部分负载下亏。`AutoHedge`（`PEGAINFER_SPEC_HEDGE_AUTO=1`）的答案是把链数交给一个**在线控制器**：周期性地把每个候选 `C ∈ {0..=Cmax}`（位置表的前缀）各跑一段「窗口」，按窗口内**实际交付的 committed tokens/sec** 打分，提交给中位数最优者；提交过期后重新探索，跟随负载漂移。

设计的两个聪明之处：

1. **优化目标就是业务目标本身**（每秒提交 token 数），于是 bucket 量化、eager 惩罚、host 开销全部被自动计价，不需要为它们建模。
2. **提交偏向便宜配置**：更大的链数必须以 `ADD_CHAIN_MARGIN = 1.03` 的优势击败当前最优才被选中——平坦地形上 argmax 是噪声，不确定性向少链方向消解。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
初始化: stats[Cmax+1] 个 CandidateStats; cur_c=0; window_rounds=WINDOW_ROUNDS(64)

每轮 verify 后 tick(executed_c, committed_tokens):
  Δt = 本轮与上轮 host 时间戳差
  if Δt > ROUND_GAP_CUTOFF(500ms): 清空当前窗口并返回   # prefill/入场停顿是调度边界，不计价
  if 本窗口首轮: window_c = executed_c
  elif executed_c ≠ window_c: 丢弃半成品窗口，重开       # 窗口只记"整窗同构"的轮
  累计 (tokens, secs); rounds_in_window += 1
  窗口满(64 轮): push 进 stats[window_c].windows，只留 MAX_WINDOWS(12) 个

探索: cur_c 走完 0..=Cmax 一圈记 1 cycle；EXPLORE_CYCLES(3) 圈后提交:
  best = 0; for c in 1..=Cmax: 若 median_rate(c) > best_rate × 1.03 → best = c
  committed = Some(best); commit_left = COMMIT_ROUNDS(4096)

提交期: current_c() 返回 committed；commit_left 耗尽 → 解除提交，
  cycles 清零，window_rounds 降为 REEXPLORE_WINDOW_ROUNDS(32) 重新探索

gated 轮（负载门退化为单 token verify）: break_window()——切断计时窗口，
  该区间永不被记到任何链数头上
```

窗口速率用**中位数**而非求和 pooling：一个被污染的窗口（图预热、拖尾请求）无法像总和那样左右提交。每个候选保留最近 12 个窗口且不加权——长提交期后现任者的窗口全是新数据、挑战者是旧数据，这**有意**偏向再次探索现任者。

与车道其余策略的关系：`PEGAINFER_SPEC_HEDGE_KNEE` 的批自适应策略**优先于**控制器（4.1.3 已见分派顺序）；控制器只在 DFlash/DSpark 车道存在（`spec_hedge_auto() && hedge_cap > 0` 才构造，[src/executor/dflash_lane.rs:L84-L88](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_lane.rs#L84-L88)）。

批自适应链数的几何约束（控制器之外的另一条路）：

\[ \text{spans} = b(1+C), \quad \text{spans} \times (\text{block}+1) \le \text{knee\_rows}, \quad \text{spans} \in \text{BATCH\_BUCKETS} \]

即扩展后的验证批既要留在 roofline 免费区（权重带宽受限、加行近乎免费）内，又要落在已捕获的 CUDA Graph bucket 上——两个 bucket 之间的跨度数会退 eager，把 hedge 收益吐回去。取满足双约束的最大 `C`；都不满足则 `C=0` 淡回基线。分数剩余（如 8 请求共容 4 条额外链）**故意不花**：唯一的中间跨度都在 bucket 外。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `break_window` 要在 gated 轮调用，而不是把 gated 轮记作 `C=0` 的正常轮？

**答案**：gated 轮是单 token verify（负载门触发），它根本不在 hedge 的配置空间里。若记作 `C=0`，会把门控期的吞吐喂给无 hedge 候选当成绩，同时推进探索/提交计数器——控制器会在错误的证据上做决定。切断窗口让该区间既不计价也不推进，回来后的第一个 tick 只重新锚定时间戳。

**练习 2**：手推 `AutoHedge::new(3)` 在「所有 C 每轮都交付 25 个 token」的平坦地形上最终提交到哪个 C？为什么？

**答案**：提交到 `C=0`。每个候选的窗口速率完全相同，提交走查从 `C=0`（中位速率 best）开始，任何更大 C 的速率都不会超过 `best_rate × 1.03`，于是 best 停在 0。这正是 `ADD_CHAIN_MARGIN` 的设计意图：平坦地形上 argmax 是噪声，不确定性向更便宜的配置消解（对应单测 `flat_landscape_settles_cheap`）。

**练习 3**：`batch_adaptive_chains(2, 7, 96, 7, BATCH_BUCKETS)` 返回什么？（block=7、knee=96 行、最多 7 链）

**答案**：span=8 行；`b(1+C)×8 ≤ 96 ⇒ b(1+C) ≤ 12`。b=2 时 `2(1+C) ∈ {2,4,8}`（bucket 集内 ≤12 的值），最大为 8 ⇒ `C=3`——注意不是免费区内最大的 C=5（10 跨度不在 bucket 上）。这是单测 `batch_adaptive_chains_picks_the_largest_bucket_aligned_count_under_the_knee` 的第二个断言。

### 4.4 spec_env 校验与投机旋钮全景

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

`spec_env.rs` 只管两个旋钮：`PEGAINFER_SPEC_MAX_BATCH`（负载门）与 `PEGAINFER_SPEC_MAX_DRAFTS`（草稿数截断）。它们共享一套刻意的语义：unset / 空白 / 显式 `0` 都是关；**任何无法解析的值在引擎启动时点名报错**，而不是静默当作关。理由写在模块文档里：静默回退会让一个「负载杠杆」变成看起来已布防的 no-op。

有趣的是对照：hedge 家族旋钮（`HEDGE`/`HEDGE_POSITIONS`/`HEDGE_AUTO`/`HEDGE_KNEE`）的文档行为恰是「unparsable = off」的静默回退（各自 OnceLock 里 `.ok().unwrap_or(0)` 一类解析），只是把**生效**几何打进启动日志补偿可见性（4.1.3）。差别在于两类旋钮的失配代价：MAX_BATCH/MAX_DRAFTS 是服务运营者按容量规划拧的负载闸，拧错了引擎还在跑、只是行为错了且难以察觉——所以必须当场拒绝；hedge 是纯性能实验旋钮，回退到 off 是安全的保守态。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

```text
引擎入口（lib.rs 两个 start 函数）
  └─ spec_env::validate()            # 先于一切装载：坏值 → 启动失败，报错含变量名
       └─ 对 MAX_BATCH、MAX_DRAFTS 各跑 parse(env_value(name))
  ……（模型装载、执行器构建）……
首次使用处（OnceLock 惰性读，每进程一次）
  ├─ plan::spec_max_batch()          # scheduler/plan.rs 的负载门
  └─ dflash::MAX_DRAFTS 截断         # effective_drafts()
```

`read()` 内部是 `.expect("spec knobs are validated before the engine starts")`——把「已校验」变成硬不变量：校验漏掉某个入口属于 bug 而非用户输入错误。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`PEGAINFER_SPEC_MAX_BATCH=8x`（多了个 x）的引擎会发生什么？`PEGAINFER_SPEC_HEDGE=8x` 呢？

**答案**：前者**拒绝启动**，报错文本含 `PEGAINFER_SPEC_MAX_BATCH: expected a non-negative integer, got "8x"`——validate() 在引擎入口第一行执行。后者静默视为 0（hedge 关闭）——`spec_hedge_cap` 的解析是 `.ok().unwrap_or(0)`，文档明写「unparsable = off」；启动日志里不会出现 "spec hedge on" 行，这是发现它没生效的线索。

**练习 2**：为什么 `read()` 里用 `expect` 直接 panic 是可接受的设计？

**答案**：因为两个引擎入口函数（`start_engine_with_offload` / `start_engine_with_lora_control`）都在第一行调用 `validate()`，任何合法路径到达 `read()` 时值必然已通过解析。此时 panic 表达的是「不变量被打破」（某个入口漏了校验），属于程序 bug 而非用户输入，fail-loud 恰是想要的行为。

**练习 3**：`--eagle3-draft-model-path` 与 `--dflash-draft-model-path` 同时给的报错出自哪一层？为什么两层都要写？

**答案**：正常 CLI 启动下第一层 `model_line.rs` 的 eagle3 冲突表先报（`--eagle3-draft-model-path is not supported with --dflash-draft-model-path`）。第二层 `lib.rs` 的折叠 match（`(Some(_), Some(_)) → bail!("DFlash and EAGLE-3 drafters cannot be loaded together")`）兜住绕过 CLI、直接构造 `Qwen3LaunchOptions` 的调用方（测试、嵌入式启动器）。同一不变量多层设防、失败越早越便宜——u1-l3 建立的原则在这里再次出现。

### 第三步：解释共享无损性判定

阅读 [tests/common/lossless.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/lossless.rs)（af9e40e1 从 `dflash_speculative_gate.rs` 抽出），写一段说明，必须覆盖：

1. **为什么精确匹配是错误的门**（[L1-L8](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/lossless.rs#L1-L8)）：verify 走 prefill 注意力核、朴素解码走 decode 核，两者差约 1 bf16 ULP，近平局处 argmax 翻转后两条贪心序列完全分岔——精确断言会**伪失败**。
2. **regret 判定的三段逻辑**（[check_lossless，L93-L216](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/lossless.rs#L93-L216)）：取首个分歧点（此刻两序列上下文仍相同，比较有效）→ 用 `prefill_next` 重算共享上下文的 **prefill 核**参考分布 → spec 选的 token 若等于 prefill argmax 则是核间隙翻转（非 bug）；否则若它距 prefill argmax 的 regret ≤ `MARGIN_TOL=0.20`（约 3 个 bf16 ULP）则是良性近平局；再否则（落在 top-K 之外或明显更差）才是真投机 bug。
3. **谁在用它**：[dflash_speculative_gate.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/dflash_speculative_gate.rs#L70-L74) 与 [eagle3_speculative_gate.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/eagle3_speculative_gate.rs#L37-L41) 现在 import 同一份 `common::lossless::{LOGPROBS, Step, check_lossless, generate, to_steps}`——两个草稿器的方法不同，但「贪心投机必须无损、且无损的定义必须容忍核间隙」这个判定完全共享。这正是 u6-l1「只有 proposer 不同」在测试层的镜像。
4. 顺带记录：DFlash 门测试的 `launch_options` 现在需要显式填 `eagle3_draft_model_path: None`（[dflash_speculative_gate.rs:L115-L139](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/dflash_speculative_gate.rs#L115-L139)）——第二草稿器加入后启动选项结构体多了一个槽位。

两个门测试本身需要 GPU + 双份权重（`PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` + `PEGAINFER_DFLASH_TEST_MODEL_PATH` / `PEGAINFER_EAGLE3_TEST_MODEL_PATH`），缺权重时按 u1-l2 的模式 clean skip，不是失败。

## 6. 本讲小结

- **草稿车道与目标同线程**是所有权与边界的双重选择：草稿 rollout 直接读目标的嵌入/输出头/捕获隐藏态，隐藏态留在车道内（`pending_context` 私有），调度器只见纯 token——`LocalQwen3Lane` 上 `dflash`/`eagle3` 两个互斥槽位是这条边界在类型上的落实。
- **`prefill_capture_supported` 已从 DFlash 专属推广为两种草稿器共享的「干净隐藏态」谓词**（无 LoRA、无前缀命中、无两种 logprobs；采样参数故意不是门），EAGLE-3 在其上叠加贪心与整段约束；prefill 后的三态动作表 MarkReady/KeepPending/Drop 由 executor 统一消费，写入 `draft_ready_requests` 就绪集。
- **`AutoHedge` 是窗口化 explore-then-commit 控制器**：按候选 C 的 64 轮窗口、以业务目标本身（committed tokens/sec 的中位数）定价，3 圈探索后向便宜方向偏置（×1.03 裕量）提交，4096 轮后重探索；500ms 间隔切断窗口、gated 轮 break_window、守卫降级轮记实际执行链数，三道防污染。
- **旋钮语义分两档**：`MAX_BATCH`/`MAX_DRAFTS` 走 `spec_env` 的「坏值点名拒绝启动」（入口第一行 validate，read 用 expect 把已校验升格为不变量）；hedge 家族是「unparsable=off」的实验旋钮，靠启动日志的生效几何补偿可见性；批自适应 `KNEE` 优先于 auto 控制器，链数受「免费区行数 ∧ CUDA Graph bucket」双约束。
- **CLI 互斥双层设防**：model_line 在启动最早期拒绝（含 EAGLE-3 的冲突表循环），lib.rs 折叠双草稿路径为单槽 `DraftModel` 兜住程序化构造；装载任一草稿器结构性关闭前缀缓存，batch-invariant 的拒绝文案已推广为 speculative。
- **`tests/common/lossless.rs` 把无损性判定抽成共享模块**：regret 检查容忍 prefill/decode 核的 1-ULP 平局翻转，同时服务 DFlash 与 EAGLE-3 两个门测试——测试层与运行时层同步完成了「共享事务、可换 proposer」的重构。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

- **u6-l8（EAGLE-3 车道与门控）**：本讲的直接续篇——`Eagle3LaneState` 如何复用 `prefill_capture_supported` 与 `DropDraft` 命令，`max_draft_batch=Some(1)` 如何在 `speculation_decision_at` 里让宽批退回纯解码，以及 `eagle3_speculative_gate.rs` 四组行为测试如何使用本讲的 lossless 判定。
- 若想再深一层验证理解：对照 [src/executor/dflash_lane.rs:L696-L710](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/dflash_lane.rs#L696-L710) 的 `select_hedged_requests`，解释「draft 与 verify 从同一列表选取」如何防止采样请求或预算饥饿请求烧掉一个 verify 侧会拒绝的 hedge 槽位——这是 u6-l4 hedge 语义在车道侧的收口。
- 回望 u4-l2 的 `speculation_decision_at`，把本讲的 `max_draft_batch` 门、`draft_ready_requests`（由本讲三态表驱动）与负载门三者的检查顺序画成一张判定流程图，作为投机子系统的总复习。

# 草稿车道集成与投机调优旋钮

> 讲义 id：u6-l7 · 层级：advanced · 依赖：u6-l2（DFlash 草稿模型）、u6-l6（verify 前向缓冲与分段 CUDA Graph）

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 解释 DFlash 草稿车道（lane）为什么必须与目标模型同住一条 worker 线程，以及「隐藏态不出车道」这条边界是如何在类型与借用结构上落实的。
2. 读懂 `dflash_prefill_action` 的三态决策表（MarkReady / KeepPending / Drop），并说出 `prefill_capture_supported` 在 af9e40e1 之后如何从 DFlash 专属谓词推广为两种草稿器（DFlash 与 EAGLE-3）共享的捕获资格判断。
3. 描述 `AutoHedge` 控制器的窗口化 explore-then-commit 设计：探索什么、按什么目标定价、如何提交、如何应对窗口污染与负载门打断。
4. 汇总全部投机旋钮（`PEGAINFER_SPEC_*` 环境变量与 `--dflash-draft-model-path` / `--eagle3-draft-model-path` CLI 标志）的作用面、默认值、读取时机与互斥规则，并理解 `spec_env` 为何对其中两个旋钮选择「坏值拒绝启动」而非静默回退。
5. 说明 `tests/common/lossless.rs` 抽出的共享无损性判定如何同时服务 DFlash 与 EAGLE-3 两个投机门测试。

## 2. 前置知识

- **车道（lane）与 worker 线程**（u3-l2）：`LocalQwen3Lane` 把一台 GPU 的全部可变状态打包，独占一条 worker 线程；executor 线程通过 `StepCommand`（算什么）与 `WorkerCommand`（控制面）两条通道与它通信。本讲的「草稿车道」就住在这个结构里。
- **投机解码事务**（u6-l1）：propose → verify → accept → commit/rollback。草稿/验证边界是**纯 token 跨界**——proposer 的隐藏态不越线。本讲讲的是「线内」的那一侧。
- **draft_ready_requests 就绪集**（u3-l1/u4-l2）：executor 侧维护的「哪些请求已捕获目标隐藏态、可以进入草稿轮」集合；调度器的 `speculation_decision_at` 全有-or-全无门控以它为输入。
- **hedge（对冲）与 DSpark**（u6-l4）：在 DFlash backbone 上叠加 Markov 头后，可以同时在多个「第二名」分支上 rollout 多条草稿链，验证阶段并行展开。链数 `C` 是个难拍脑袋定的性能参数——这正是 4.3 节自定价控制器的动机。
- **OnceLock 一次性读取**：所有 `PEGAINFER_SPEC_*` 旋钮每个进程只读一次环境变量，之后缓存为静态值——运行中改环境变量不会生效。
